canonical_name: Sperner's maximum-size theorem for a finite Boolean lattice
canonical_statement: For every finite ground set of cardinality n, an antichain of its subsets has maximum possible cardinality choose(n, floor(n/2)): a lower-middle-layer antichain attains that cardinality, and every antichain has cardinality at most it.

source_selection.repository_claim: Docs/researches/math_theorems.md:6033-6038: maximum size of an antichain in a power set
source_selection.citation: Emanuel Sperner, Ein Satz uber Untermengen einer endlichen Menge, Mathematische Zeitschrift 27 (1928), 544-548, DOI 10.1007/BF01171114
source_selection.variant_decision: The catalog literally asks for a maximum size, so the root includes both a universal sharp upper bound and an attaining antichain. An upper bound alone would not establish a maximum. The paper's additional classification of all equality families is stronger than the catalog gloss and is not silently added to this root.
source_selection.review_boundary: The source scan and intake crosswalk support this provisional variant decision, but accountable translation, complete proof mapping, corrections or errata review, independent H0 review, and master acceptance remain open.

domain_and_universes: At arbitrary universe u: alpha : Type u with Fintype alpha; A : Finset (Finset alpha); propositions remain in Lean universe 0.
hypotheses: for the universal bound, distinct members of A are incomparable under Finset subset
conclusion: There exists an antichain with cardinality Nat.choose (Fintype.card alpha) (Fintype.card alpha / 2), and every antichain has cardinality at most that value.

encoding_decisions.ground_set: An arbitrary finite type alpha; the theorem depends only on Fintype.card alpha and therefore covers every finite labeled ground set without fixing Fin n.
encoding_decisions.family: A finite family Finset (Finset alpha). Every subset of a finite type has a Finset representative, and duplicate family members are absent by construction.
encoding_decisions.antichain: IsAntichain (fun x y : Finset alpha => x subset y) on the coerced family; IsAntichain tests distinct members, matching the source's phrase that no member is a subset of another such member.
encoding_decisions.maximum: Attainability and the upper bound are conjoined. The checked alternate chooses the concrete lower middle layer powersetCard (card alpha / 2) univ as witness.
encoding_decisions.middle_rank: Natural-number division card alpha / 2 is floor(n/2). For odd n the upper middle layer has the same size, but is not needed for the maximum-value claim.
encoding_decisions.boundary: Empty and singleton ground types, empty and singleton families, and both parities are included. The concrete lower-middle witness is {empty} for Fin 0 and Fin 1.
encoding_decisions.equality_classification: The stronger statement that these are the only equality families, with the even/odd cases on source page 544, is not a credited alternate and remains downstream source/proof work if the integration lane expands the root.

minimal_import_result: The canonical target definitions elaborate with the sole direct import and fail when it is removed. The complete statement/transport module also elaborates. The proof-bearing Mathlib.Combinatorics.SetFamily.LYM module and IsAntichain.sperner are deliberately not imported or credited by the statement phase.
minimal_import_boundary: This establishes necessity among the declared imports for the canonical target fixture. It does not claim that no differently factored collection of lower mathlib modules has a smaller transitive closure.

alternate_encodings.boundary: The alternate replaces only the existential attaining family with the explicit lower middle layer; it retains the identical universal upper-bound component.
